model.title: How does Shakespeare present the effects of guilt on Lady Macbeth?

parts.text: Thesis: guilt dismantles the control Lady Macbeth once commanded
Extract: 'Out, damned spot!': the imperative now has no power
Contrast: Act 1 'unsex me here' asked spirits for strength
Context: Jacobean belief that conscience and God's judgement cannot be escaped

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Shakespeare presents guilt as dismantling the control Lady Macbeth once commanded: her imperative 'Out, damned spot!' is powerless, a bitter echo of Act 1, when she called on spirits to 'unsex' her.
